title: 2004 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: In \(\triangle ABC\) points \(D\) and \(E\) lie on \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{AC},\) respectively. If \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{BE}\) intersect at \(T\) so that \(\frac{AT}{DT} = 3\) and \(\frac{BT}{ET} = 4,\) what is \(\frac{CD}{BD}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(F\) be on \(\overline{AC}\) with \(DF \parallel BE,\) and write \(ET = x,\) \(BT = 4x.\)

From \(\triangle ATE \sim \triangle ADF,\) \(\dfrac{DF}{x} = \dfrac{AD}{AT} = \dfrac{4}{3},\) so \(DF = \dfrac{4x}{3}.\)

From \(\triangle BEC \sim \triangle DFC,\) \(\dfrac{CD}{BC} = \dfrac{DF}{BE} = \dfrac{\frac{4x}{3}}{5x} = \dfrac{4}{15}.\)

Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} \dfrac{CD}{BD} &= \dfrac{\frac{CD}{BC}}{1 - \frac{CD}{BC}} \\ &= \dfrac{\frac{4}{15}}{\frac{11}{15}} = \dfrac{4}{11}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Draw the line through \(D\) parallel to \(\overline{BE}\) meeting \(\overline{AC}\) at a point \(F\)
Two pairs of similar triangles give \(\frac{CD}{BC},\) which converts to \(\frac{CD}{BD}\)
